newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish fund to place two more firms on the bourse.
newsitem.headline: Polish fund to place two more firms on the bourse.

text.p: The Polish National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 13 plans to place two more companies from its portfolio on the Warsaw bourse this year, the fund said on Wednesday.
The fund, one of 15 such institution created under Poland's mass privatisation programme, said in a statement it would seek listing for textile maker Bielbaw SA and leather company Skotan SA.
"In 1997, shares of Bielbaw and Skotan will enter the bourse," it said.
The two public offerings and two other previously announced -- of paint maker Polifarb Debica SA and chemical firm Viscoplast SA -- would be worth a total of 54 million zlotys.
The statement also said that construction firm Pekabex SA and mining machines maker Nowomag SA would be listed on over-the-counter market.
Strategic investors will be sought for transport company Cemet SA, cement producer Cementownia Rejowiec SA and feed maker Przedsiebiorstwo Przemylu Paszowego Ilpasz SA, it said.
The fund had a net loss of 30.8 million zlotys last year, compared with a 1.2 million loss in 1995.
